item.title: Phelan Confirmed to Lead Trump’s Council of Economic Advisers
item.description: The US Senate confirmed Christopher Phelan, a former adviser to the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, as chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers.

item.title: US Sanctions Iranian Digital Exchanges as Trump Promises Deal
item.description: The US ramped up economic pressure on Iran with more sanctions on digital asset exchanges and networks connected to the country’s shadow-banking system, as President Donald Trump says Washington and Tehran are coming close to an agreement.

item.title: US Treasury Sparks Debate Over Auction Cutbacks to Temper Yields
item.description: The US Treasury triggered debate this week about something that’s for years been an article of faith about the world’s biggest bond market: the government’s auctions of notes and bonds will just have to keep getting bigger.

item.title: DraftKings CEO Blasts Prediction Bets on Earnings Call Comments
item.description: DraftKings Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jason Robins said he doesn’t think it is good that bettors are placing prediction market wagers on what executives say on company earnings calls.

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Some Work on New Astra Model Over Cyber Concerns
item.description: OpenAI is pausing some internal work around one of its upcoming artificial intelligence models to implement stricter safeguards after the system was found to be significantly more adept at cybersecurity tasks.

item.title: Why Take-Two Won’t Share ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Pre-Order Numbers
item.description: CEO Strauss Zelnick says he doesn’t want to mislead shareholders

item.title: The Free Money AI Bond Buildout Is Gone
item.description: Hyperscaler debt funding is getting pricier.

item.title: Trump Tariffs ‘Tortuous’ to Soybean Trade, China Diplomat Says
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s trade war with China created a “tortuous experience” that disrupted the flow of soybeans between the world’s two largest economies, a Chinese diplomat said Friday.

item.title: Congo to Investigate Reports of Excess Uranium in Cobalt Exports
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo will look into reports of excess uranium leaving the country in its exports of battery mineral cobalt, the government said Thursday.

item.title: BlackRock’s Rieder Sees AI Helping Buoy GDP Even as Hiring Slows
item.description: BlackRock Inc.’s Rick Rieder said last month’s surprise contraction in payrolls reflects a “productivity revolution” rather than economic weakness, arguing that the US economy remains on track for 6% nominal growth in gross domestic product even as hiring stalls.

item.title: EU Accelerates Sovereign Satellite Plans Citing Defense Needs
item.description: The European Union said it’s bulking up plans for a sovereign satellite constellation and will accelerate its service launch by a year to 2029, citing a changing security environment that will require greater communication capacity.

item.title: Fitch Sees Chile Budget as Key to Halting Rising Debt Burden
item.description: Fitch Ratings is skeptical that tax cuts approved by Chile’s Congress last month will boost growth by enough to offset the immediate drop in revenue, leaving the emphasis on fiscal spending reductions if the government wants to balance the books anytime soon.

item.title: Worst-Ever Brazil Market Outage Puts B3’s Near-Monopoly in Focus
item.description: The worst trading outage ever in Brazilian financial markets was just the latest disruption over the past year to bedevil investors in Latin America’s biggest economy.

item.title: QVC Issues $1.2 Billion of 10% Yield Debt as It Exits Bankruptcy
item.description: QVC Group has issued $1.2 billion in so-called take-back debt as part of its emergence from Chapter 11 bankruptcy, with the TV shopping network looking to grow its digital footprint.

item.title: Once-AAA Bonds on New York Megamall Face Over $350 Million Loss
item.description: Pyramid Management Group, a shopping center developer, is buying back the mortgage on a struggling megamall it owns in Syracuse, New York, for cents on the dollar, mostly wiping out bonds that originally carried top ratings.

item.title: CFTC Warns Prediction Markets Against American-Style Casino Odds
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission told prediction markets to avoid using American-style gambling odds as the US regulator fends off legal challenges alleging the platforms are illicit sports betting operations.

item.title: Dollar Falls to Lowest Level Since May as Rate Hike in Doubt
item.description: The dollar fell Friday after soft US labor data reduced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in the near term.

item.title: Fed’s Barkin Says Labor in ‘Weak Balance,’ Not Fueling Prices
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Tom Barkin said the labor market appears to be in a “weak balance,” continuing the low-hire environment that has been in place for the past year.

item.title: Veritas-Backed Firm Begins Year’s Biggest Software Refinancing
item.description: Gainwell Technologies has kicked off a $5.8 billion debt overhaul that would be the US software sector’s biggest of 2026, doing so as the sector has underperformed the broader leveraged-loan market by the most in years.

item.title: Ukraine Grain Exports to Slump After Russian Strikes on Odesa
item.description: Ukraine’s agricultural shipments could fall by more than half this season after Russian attacks disrupted Black Sea ports, threatening the country’s biggest source of export revenue.

item.title: Hungary Warns of Dramatic Hit From Drought, Nuclear Outage
item.description: Hungary is facing a “dramatic” economic impact given the drought across its agricultural heartland, combined with what may turn out to be a lengthy nuclear production outage, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said.

item.title: Puerto Rico’s Capital Sees Blowout Demand for Rare Muni Sale
item.description: San Juan, the economic hub of Puerto Rico, triggered a rush for its $121 million muni-bond sale this week, as investors seized a rare opportunity to get exposure to island.

item.description: Here are the key takeaways from the US employment report for July, released Friday:

item.title: SK Hynix Is Said to Mull Options for $3 Billion Chongqing Assets
item.description: South Korea’s SK Hynix Inc. is considering options for its Chongqing, China-based facility, including bringing in an investor to help accelerate growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Yen Jumps 1% Against Dollar After US Jobs Data
item.description: The yen surged against the dollar after US jobs data, after earlier speculation in markets that authorities could intervene again on the currency.

item.title: US Treasuries Rally as Soft Jobs Data Trims Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: US Treasuries rallied after data showed employers unexpectedly cut jobs in July, suggesting labor market challenges that could impact the Federal Reserve’s willingness to raise interest rates.

item.title: US Employers Unexpectedly Shed Jobs; Unemployment Rate Falls
item.description: US employers unexpectedly cut jobs in July and hiring in the prior two months was revised lower, suggesting the labor market is weaker than previously thought after surprising strength earlier this year.

item.title: Canada Adds 75,100 Jobs, Unemployment Rate Hits Two-Year Low
item.description: The Canadian economy added a surprise 75,100 jobs last month while the unemployment rate hit its lowest level in two years — the latest evidence the economy is on a recovery path.

item.title: Chile Consumer Prices Inch Up in July as Fuel Pressures Fade
item.description: Chile’s consumer prices posted a muted gain in July as a drop in fuel costs at the start of the month provided some inflation relief to one of Latin America’s richest economies.

item.title: Garbage-Truck Margin Boost Shows the AI Profit Boom Has Begun
item.description: Corporate America’s adoption of artificial intelligence tools is paying off, in a major relief to investors who had questioned massive investments in the technology by a concentrated number of companies.
